questions.question_text: Which description gives the complete graph of $f(x) = \begin{cases} x + 4, & x < 0 \\ 4 - 2x, & x \ge 0 \end{cases}$?

options.text: A line of slope $1$ extends left from $(0,4)$ through $(-4,0)$, and a line of slope $-2$ extends right from $(0,4)$ through $(2,0)$; the join at $(0,4)$ is filled.
A line of slope $1$ extends left from $(0,4)$ through $(-4,0)$, and a line of slope $-2$ extends right from $(0,4)$ through $(2,0)$; the join at $(0,4)$ is open.
options.why: Excluded $x = 0$ from both branches despite the inclusive inequality $x \ge 0$.

options.text: A line of slope $1$ extends left from $(0,4)$ through $(-4,0)$, and a line of slope $2$ extends right from $(0,4)$ through $(2,8)$; the join at $(0,4)$ is filled.
options.why: Changed the right branch from $4 - 2x$ to $4 + 2x$, reversing its slope.

options.text: A line of slope $-2$ extends left from $(0,4)$ through $(-2,8)$, and a line of slope $1$ extends right from $(0,4)$ through $(2,6)$; the join at $(0,4)$ is filled.
options.why: Applied $4 - 2x$ on the left and $x + 4$ on the right, swapping the branches' intervals.
Used a line of slope $+1$ instead of slope $-1$ for $x \le 0$.
Reversed the open and closed endpoint inequalities at $x = 0$.
Used a concave-down parabola $1 - x^{2}$ instead of the concave-up parabola $x^{2} + 1$.

questions.solution_text:
For $x \le 0$, the graph is the line $y = -x$ ending at $(0,0)$ with a filled dot.
For $x > 0$, the graph is the parabola $y = x^{2} + 1$ starting at $(0,1)$ with an open circle.
Rule: $f(x) = \begin{cases} -x, & x \le 0 \\ x^{2} + 1, & x > 0 \end{cases}$

questions.question_text: Find the range of the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} -3x^{2}, & x < 0 \\ 4x, & x \ge 0 \end{cases}$.

options.why: Only accounted for the right branch $4x \ge 0$, ignoring the negative outputs from $-3x^{2}$.
Only accounted for the left branch $-3x^{2} < 0$, ignoring the positive outputs from $4x$.
Excluded $y = 0$, but $f(0) = 4(0) = 0$ is included in the range.

questions.solution_text:
For $x < 0$, $y = -3x^{2} < 0$, giving outputs $(-\infty, 0)$.
For $x \ge 0$, $y = 4x \ge 0$, giving outputs $[0, \infty)$.
The union of these outputs is $(-\infty, 0) \cup [0, \infty) = (-\infty, \infty)$.

questions.question_text: Which description correctly matches the graph of the piecewise function $f(x) = \begin{cases} 3x - 4, & x \le 2 \\ 7 - x^{2}, & x > 2 \end{cases}$?

options.text: A line with positive slope ending with a filled dot at $(2,2)$, and a downward-opening parabola starting with an open circle at $(2,3)$.
A line with positive slope ending with an open circle at $(2,2)$, and a downward-opening parabola starting with a filled dot at $(2,3)$.
options.why: Attached the filled dot to the strict inequality $x > 2$ and the open circle to $x \le 2$, reversing the endpoint convention.

options.text: A line with positive slope ending with a filled dot at $(2,2)$, and an upward-opening parabola starting with an open circle at $(2,3)$.
options.why: Read $7 - x^{2}$ as having a positive leading coefficient, so treated the parabola as upward-opening instead of downward-opening.

options.text: A line with positive slope ending with an open circle at $(2,2)$, and an upward-opening parabola starting with a filled dot at $(2,3)$.
options.why: Read $7 - x^{2}$ as upward-opening and also reversed the endpoint convention, filling the dot for $x > 2$ instead of for $x \le 2$.

questions.solution_text:
For $x \le 2$, $y = 3x - 4$ is a line with positive slope $3$ that terminates at $(2, 3(2) - 4) = (2,2)$ with a filled dot because the inequality is $\le$.
For $x > 2$, $y = 7 - x^{2}$ is a downward-opening parabola that starts at $(2, 7 - 2^{2}) = (2,3)$ with an open circle because the inequality is $>$.
Therefore, the graph consists of a line with positive slope ending with a filled dot at $(2,2)$, and a downward-opening parabola starting with an open circle at $(2,3)$.

options.why: Used open brackets instead of closed brackets, excluding the reachable values $\pm 2$.
Assumed the horizontal rays extend vertically to infinity.
Only listed the constant horizontal values, ignoring the connected line segment.

questions.solution_text:
The lowest $y$-value on the graph is $-2$ and the highest is $2$.
Every value between $-2$ and $2$ is attained on the segment $[-1, 1]$.
$\text{Range} = [-2, 2]$

questions.question_text:
A piecewise function is defined on $[-3, 5]$ by $f(x) = \begin{cases} x + 2, & -3 \le x < 1 \\ 4 - x, & 1 \le x \le 5 \end{cases}$.
What is the range of $f(x)$?

options.why: Excluded $y = 3$ because $x = 1$ is outside the first branch, missing that the second branch gives $f(1) = 4 - 1 = 3$.
Copied the smallest domain value $-3$ as the smallest $y$-value instead of evaluating $f(-3) = -3 + 2 = -1$.
Copied the domain's left endpoint $-3$ as the minimum $y$-value and also excluded $y = 3$, overlooking that $f(1) = 3$.

questions.solution_text:
For $-3 \le x < 1$, $y = x + 2$ ranges from $-3 + 2 = -1$ up to $1 + 2 = 3$ (open): $[-1, 3)$.
For $1 \le x \le 5$, $y = 4 - x$ ranges from $4 - 5 = -1$ up to $4 - 1 = 3$ (closed): $[-1, 3]$.
The combined range is $[-1, 3]$.

questions.question_text: Find the range of $f(x) = \begin{cases} x + 2, & x < -2 \\ x - 2, & x > 3 \end{cases}$.

options.why: Included the boundary outputs $0$ and $1$ despite both branch inequalities being strict.
Filled the gap between the branch ranges, although neither branch produces any value in $[0,1]$.
Reported the input intervals instead of calculating the output intervals.

questions.solution_text:
For $x < -2$, $y = x + 2 < 0$, giving outputs $(-\infty,0)$.
For $x > 3$, $y = x - 2 > 1$, giving outputs $(1,\infty)$.
Both boundary values are excluded.
$\text{Range} = (-\infty,0) \cup (1,\infty)$.

questions.question_text: Find the range of $f(x) = \begin{cases} x + 1, & x < -2 \\ x^{2} + 2, & -1 \le x \le 2 \\ x + 3, & x > 4 \end{cases}$.

options.why: Used only the quadratic branch's endpoint values $3$ and $6$, missing its minimum $2$ at $x = 0$.
Included the excluded boundary outputs $-1$ and $7$ from the strict outer inequalities.
Joined the middle and right branch ranges across the unattained values in $(6,7]$.

questions.solution_text:
For $x < -2$, $y = x + 1 < -1$, giving outputs $(-\infty,-1)$.
On $-1 \le x \le 2$, $y = x^{2} + 2$ has its minimum $2$ at $x = 0$. Its endpoint values are $f(-1) = 3$ and $f(2) = 6$, so this branch gives $[2,6]$.
For $x > 4$, $y = x + 3 > 7$, giving outputs $(7,\infty)$.
$\text{Range} = (-\infty,-1) \cup [2,6] \cup (7,\infty)$.
